## X. The Unfunded Successor

By August, Lovelace could work for an hour and lose the afternoon to it.

The arithmetic of her illness was more exact than its cause. A journey to
London spent several days. A long letter spent one. Visitors spent whatever
strength courtesy concealed from them. At Ockham, papers from the Calculation
Office arrived in packets whose urgency was visible before she broke their
seals.

William found her with the capacity qualification, Neale's checking sheets, and
three letters spread over the bed.

“You promised me one hour,” he said.

“I said I would not travel.”

“You promised both.”

He removed none of the papers. He set the water within her reach and drew the
curtains against the light.

“They have made checking depend upon a single man,” she said.

“Then it does not depend upon you.”

“It depends upon my continuing to insist that he is single.”

Her signature stood alone beside the claim clauses in the copy before her.
Beneath it, *deputy, if required* was still legible through the line she had
drawn. She set one finger on it.

“Would you have signed it?” she asked.

“What?”

“If they had put your name there.”

“I could not have done your work.”

“No.”

She drew the copy back onto her lap. A moment later she straightened it so he
could read the line.

“I would not have let you,” she said.

William sat down beside the bed. She waited for him to say that she had been
right. He asked whether the water was still cool.

She had proposed that Samuel Wills spend part of each week under Neale and part
with an assurance clerk outside the office. During training, output would fall
further. The additional wages and external review would cost approximately one
hundred and twenty pounds in the first year. Halden's answer praised the plan
and asked whether it might begin after the four current packets were delivered.
Babbage's answer proposed that recurrent portions of comparison might later be
mechanized.

She read Halden's answer again, looking for a date she could put beside the
cost. Babbage offered a route through machinery that did not yet exist. Neither paper gave her a day on which Wills would begin.

Lovelace began another page with three headings: competence, paid time,
authority to refuse. She entered Wills, Neale, Halden, Babbage, Davies, and
herself. No row was complete. She sent the unfinished table to both men and
asked them to accept no work beyond Neale's demonstrated reach until one was.

Babbage came to Ockham near the end of the month. He brought drawings rather
than the office account. She recognized the peace offering and the evasion in
the same roll of paper.

He opened the roll across her unanswered table. She drew one edge of it back
into view.

He showed her a proposed means by which a later apparatus might verify parts of
its own operation sequence.

She followed his pencil through two transfers and made him return to the carry.
At the next comparison she stopped him again: both checking paths inherited the
same earlier value. He stared at the lines, rubbed one away with his thumb, and
sent the second path through another register. She moved the delayed sign one
operation farther. He saw why before she explained it.

She left one finger where the two paths had inherited the same value. “If a
later apparatus compared enough of its own operations, would you call that
judgment?”

“Judgment is often the name we give an operation whose conditions have not yet
been exposed,” he said. “If the apparatus compares its own proceedings and
changes what follows, at what exact line would you deny it the word?”

“I wrote that an Engine might compose music if the relations of harmony could
be given to its operations. It might carry them to a passage no composer had
set down note by note.”

“Would it not have invented the passage?”

“The consequence might be new to us. The relations and purpose would still
have entered from us. Our surprise would not be its intention.”

He crossed out *verification* and wrote *comparison of internal operations*.

For several minutes the mechanism occupied the whole table. He began a mark and
she completed it; she crossed out his correction and he laughed. Their old
speed returned so suddenly that neither acknowledged it. For those minutes
William's hour ceased to exist for both of them. Then she reached for the
pencil and had to wait for her breath. When she shifted in the chair, the edge
of Guardian's source sheet slipped from beneath the roll.

“It is good,” she said.

He waited for the rest.

“It does not read Guardian's source sheet.”

She drew the successor register from beneath the roll and closed it over his
letter.

He did not consent or refuse. He recommended that the office wait. Halden
adopted the recommendation, deferring training until the present contracts
produced their next payments.

After he left, Lovelace attached his answer and Halden's to her question. She
left the page unclosed, so the unanswered place remained visible.

By November she was in Marylebone, at Great Cumberland Place, and the papers
that had once replaced her presence now had difficulty reaching her at all. She
died there on the twenty-seventh.

News reached Halden at the office before noon. He closed the preparation room
for the day and left the apparatus uncovered, because nobody could agree who
possessed the authority to alter the schedule. Neale stood beside four waiting
packets, his blank strip arrested beneath the first line. Babbage came late and
went first to the machine. He pressed his palm against the frame and left it
there. No motion returned through the metal. It was cold and still.

During 1853 the four packets passed through the office in overlapping stages.
On most days this looked like growth. Preparers borrowed desks and reused card
forms; Neale moved to whichever promised date was nearest; corrections that
once had opened a margin now consumed it. Wills's ruler and pencil moved from
packet to packet. The edge of Neale's blank strip darkened with use. No single
day announced failure; each exception was carried forward until one could leave
the room.

On 1 April 1854 Guardian's signed return arrived. Wills laid it beside the
specimen sheets. Much of the card order could be kept. Neale put the old
checking sheets aside; their ticks belonged to different figures. He drew the
first new source beneath his strip.

## XI. The Seller's Conditions

Halden's reply to Guardian contained the source sheet, the preparation copy,
the cards, both run traces, the delivery ledger, and the sentence with which he
had begun: there was no second signature.

Davies accepted the trace and rejected the table.

Clause eleven required correction at the seller's expense. The following
clause permitted cancellation if the error had passed a promised independent
check or if no such check had occurred. Guardian invoked both. Its deposit of
one hundred and eighty pounds was to be returned. The corrected table would be
received as evidence of performance under the clause, not as completion of a
continuing contract.

The office recomputed the deck. Wills copied the source under Neale's voice,
then Neale copied it again under Wills's. The apparatus produced the corrected
values. The work took four days. By the third evening Neale's voice had
roughened, and Wills read while Neale followed with the grey-edged strip.

When Neale stopped him, Wills began the whole line again, faster.

“From where the strip is.”

Wills found the place. He read the figure once. Neale moved the strip, and they
went on.

When they exchanged sheets, Wills asked for a repetition. The request came out
too softly; Neale had already begun the next figure. Wills put his pencil across the copy.

“The one before, Mr Neale.”

Neale returned to it. Wills entered the figure only after he had heard it again.
Neither man looked towards the office door. There was still the rest of the
column to read.

The correction had required no alteration to the mechanism. Babbage wanted
the response to say so.

He slid the two exact run traces away from the delivery ledger. Halden returned
them to the same packet before answering.

“Put this before the refund,” Babbage said. “The difference enters before the
first card.”

“The trace makes it clear,” Halden said.

“A trace in a cancelled office will not govern what people say. They will say
the Engine made a wrong table.”

“Guardian paid us to stop that table leaving,” Halden said. “The clerk has his
line in the trace. Mine is in the ledger. I won't answer cancellation with a
paragraph about the Engine.”

Halden opened the office account.

There had been nine hundred pounds in contributed capital and seven hundred and
twenty in customer deposits. Wages, rent, heat, cards, maintenance, and delivery
had consumed most of it. Guardian's refund, the correction, reprinting, closure,
and storage consumed the rest. Even if another customer agreed to wait, the
office could not support the staff required to complete and independently check
the remaining work without new capital.

“Then raise new capital on the investigation,” Babbage said.

“Upon what statement?”

“That the calculating mechanism executed every operation supplied to it;
preparation and checking failed outside it.”

“And the office?”

“Those functions can be constituted anew under stricter conditions.”

Halden imagined the circular. A correct machine, a corrected human process,
subscriptions sought for renewed operation under improved safeguards. Every
sentence could be defended. Together they would invite a new subscriber to
finance obligations the present account could not meet.

Margaret had sorted the figures the night before into sums already owed, money
still in hand, and money a new circular only hoped to attract. When Halden began
to call the third rescue, she put one finger beneath the first.

“Before you send another circular,” she had said, “show me what leaves this
house before the first new subscription comes in.”

New money might preserve Halden's standing and keep Wills and Neale employed.
It might also convert Guardian's disclosed error into evidence that the system
had already corrected itself. He had spent twelve years teaching other men that
a future capacity could not pay a present debt merely because it was described
well.

He wrote the closure resolution.

The remaining customer obligations would be completed only where existing
funds and independent checking sufficed; otherwise they would be cancelled
before another stage became due. Guardian would receive its refund and corrected
table. Wills and Neale would be paid through the closure month. The apparatus
would be dismantled into stored assemblies. The complete ledger would name the
February 1852 four-job authorization and the April 1854 delivery exception.
Under *cause of exception*, Halden first wrote *pressure of business*. He read
the words, struck them through, and copied both of his authorizations in full.

Wills asked to see him after the staff were told.

“Will the record carry my name?” the young man asked.

“On the preparation copy.”

“And on my reference?”

“The reference will state both the error and what you did afterward.”

Wills looked toward the preparation room. “A new master may stop at the error.”

Neale had waited at the door with his wooden case. “Put my name beneath the
correction, sir. He read the second copy. I followed.”

Halden added the sentence. Neale initialled it, then Halden turned the reference
around and placed it beside Wills's ruler. “Read it before I sign.”

On the last day of March 1855, the shaft beneath the calculating room stopped.
Farrow's men removed the card reader first, then the registers. Neale carried
his checking books away in a wooden case. Wills left with a reference that
described both the error and his conduct during correction.

Halden locked the account and gave one key to the subscriber trust's solicitor
and one to Babbage.

“You have used the stopping clauses as though dissolution were a completed
stage,” Babbage said.

“The wages are paid. The customers have their money or their work. One key goes
to the trust and one to you.”

“That preserves the account by surrendering the work.”

Halden waited. Babbage closed his hand around the key.

“It does,” Halden said.

nodes.text:
## XII. The Complete Record

In 1871, Henry Babbage found the returned table among his father's successful
papers.

It had remained there for sixteen years. At first Charles pencilled *mechanism
trace exact* upon the wrapper. Later he asked Halden for the reconciled account
and tied it beneath the same green tape. The tape had been opened often enough
to soften at the knot. Each time, proof and failure returned beneath one
fastening.

Charles had asked him to inventory what would pass into his custody. The work
occupied several autumn afternoons. Drawings had multiplied beyond cabinets.
Mechanisms stood beneath covers. Notes on improvements continued into the
present year, written in the same hand that had marked changes before Henry was
born.

The packet from the old undertaking was different. It had been assembled as if
for a dispute whose parties might all be dead. The frozen configuration came
first, then the successor register, inspection corrections, sealed cases, run
traces, and the signed statement of 1851. After them lay Lady Lovelace's
capacity qualification, her unanswered succession question, the source sheet,
the transposed copy, the delivery exception, Davies's cancellation, the
corrected table, and Halden's closure account.

Her qualification began in the close hand Henry knew from the Notes. Its final
directions stood farther apart, each beginning at the margin.

Henry lifted the returned table. “This is filed with the Engine papers.”

His father was seated near the fire, wrapped in a coat although the day was not
cold. Age had reduced the distance he could cross without effort but not the
distance his thought attempted in a sentence.

“It was not an error of the Engine,” Charles said.

Henry set it beside the office accounts.

“Not there,” Charles said.

Henry left the sheet between the two piles. “Then the inventory needs a heading
that takes both.”

For several seconds, only the fire answered.

“That was Halden's question,” Charles said at last. “What had the customer
purchased?”

“The apparatus performed the operation supplied to it. Precisely. Yet the
office had undertaken to supply a table. Lady Lovelace insisted upon that
distinction before the office existed.”

Henry kept his pencil above the blank line.

“I distinguished the general machine from a temporary arrangement of persons.”
Charles looked toward the covered mechanisms. “The distinction was true.” His
voice lost its earlier force. “It did not answer the account. The office had
undertaken to deliver a correct table.”

Henry had grown up among unfinished objects defended by future completion.
Even now the covered mechanisms drew his eye away from the account. There was
work he could imagine doing with them, and he had to bring himself back to the
blank inventory line. The returned table still lay between the two piles.
Whatever happened to the drawings, it would need a place.

Military service had taken Henry far from these rooms. Now he had returned,
with questions of his own about the machinery, and his father tired before they
could finish an argument.

Charles noticed him looking towards the drawings.

“Not that sheet. The alteration is on the next.”

Henry lifted it. Underneath lay a drawing crowded with pencilled corrections.

“Here?”

“One farther.”

Henry carried the drawing to him. They followed a line together until it passed
beneath another sheet. His father was still tracing its continuation when Henry
moved the paper aside.

“Yes,” Charles said. “You see.”

Henry returned the drawing to its place and took up the pencil beside the
inventory.

“What name shall I put upon the inventory?” Henry asked.

Charles answered too quickly. “Analytical Engine—experimental working papers.”

Henry wrote the phrase, then left space beneath it.

His father noticed. “You disapprove?”

“It does not explain why the accounts are present.”

Charles asked for the inventory. His hand was unsteady, and Henry expected him
to strike out the first line. Instead he added another.

Bounded apparatus and calculation office: configuration, proof, qualification,
error, correction, and closure, complete.

“Complete,” Henry read.

“Of that object,” Charles said. “Not of the Engine.”

“I understand.”

“Do you?”

The old impatience sharpened the words, but it could not sustain itself. Charles
rested the pen.

“No matter. Keep the sentence.”

The packet passed into Henry's custody with the drawings and workshop material
after his father's death. He copied both headings into the inventory and placed
the packet beside the drawings.

In 1900, Henry opened the packet again.

The green tape had faded. Guardian's seal remained broken along the cut Halden
made in 1854. The wrong table and the corrected one lay side by side, equally
preserved. Between them was Lovelace's qualification, its final lines still
widening toward the end.

Henry returned her sheet between the two tables and tied the faded tape around
all three.

{"schema":"meaning-model-review/v1","kind":"review","text":"# The Book of Conditions — first continuation candidate

Status: private, unaccepted editorial candidate, 27 September 2026. Nothing in the accepted source, model, paper, compiled examples, or releases has been replaced. `manuscript-v1.md` is a complete book, not a set of excerpts. This pass is local fiction editing; it introduces no claim of historical evidence.

## What the book already achieves

The manuscript has a strong causal structure: one bounded proof becomes a temptation to expand, scarce independent checking remains scarce, and the institution fails while the mechanism performs its supplied operations correctly. The return of the same physical objects — drawings, checking strip, signature, account, green tape — gives the changing interpretation a material continuity. The successful trial is allowed genuine shared joy. That matters: later division costs the characters something they actually had.

The existing refinements already resist an easy saint-and-villains reading. Lovelace protects her rare authority in a way that also makes it fragile. Halden understands the limit he exceeds. Babbage's architectural distinction is true and inadequate to the purchased obligation. These should survive expansion.

The current risk is more local than a missing plot: the narrator and principals sometimes finish the interpretation before the scene has had time to produce it. Secondary people can become bearers of the founders' lesson. Wills makes the error and receives a reference, but has little room to practice the uncertain competence that management prematurely treats as future capacity. Margaret's labor is recognized in narration, then she immediately serves the useful function of correcting Edward. More explanation would intensify those problems.

## The chosen first pass

Nine bounded changes develop existing material. The candidate adds about four hundred words overall; seven of the twelve sections change. It does not add a thirteenth section, another catastrophe, a new customer, a new failure, an improved apparatus, or a new historical assertion. Sections II, III, IV, VI and VIII remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

The largest additions occur inside the existing E17 training and E26 correction. Wills learns to stop when he cannot independently read a source; after the failure he makes himself ask Neale to repeat a figure. These are modest actions, not proof that he is now an independent checker. Neale does not become an infallible rescuer. He admits unreadability, directs the work, and accepts being interrupted. Their language stays close to the sheet.

Margaret gets one brief working boundary: Edward must wait for her to finish an entry before spreading his venture across her book. The final custody scene loses one explanatory paragraph in favor of Henry's eye returning from the tempting mechanisms to the inventory line. Lovelace's unanswered question is allowed an extra beat of searching for an actionable date.

The accepted model currently supports the parent actions and broad character interpretations. Three newly specified interactions are proposals requiring event/evidence refinement before adoption as model-grounded prose. They are not already present in the model merely because they are plausible. The other edits render established actions or substitute local scene detail for explanatory prose; they require fresh document/span identities if adopted, but not changed world causality or numerical profiles.

## Adoption map

Each `BC-` identifier is local to this editorial pass, not a native Meaning Model ID. Exact before/after text, line anchors, and SHA-256 hashes are in `scene-anchor-map.json`. Existing E-numbers below are the accepted authored event aliases; any native IDs must be resolved from the import receipt.

| Edit | Section / event | Classification | Intended effect | Required action before adopting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BC-01 | I / E25 | Prose-only elaboration | Allow Wills's silence and Halden's impulse to repeat the accusation to take time; Halden still finds his own authorization. | Rebind changed passage evidence; no new cause, accusation, or profile weight. |
| BC-02 | V / E06 | Prose-only elaboration | Replace Lovelace's universal institutional maxim with her attention to stopping clauses. | Rebind passage; retain authority and deputy decisions. |
| BC-03 | VII / E11 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Margaret finishes her own account entry before taking the venture ledger. | Extend E11 / household-work interpretation with this proposed interaction; retain the same payment and pause decision. |
| BC-04 | VII / E11, Halden's later interpretation | Prose-only elaboration | Bring the existing household exchange back into Halden's remembered proof of discipline instead of announcing a general lesson. | Rebind passage; read as attributed retrospective interpretation, not additional documentary history. |
| BC-05 | IX / E17 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Open training: unreadable source, comparison to expectation, Wills's request for the original, Neale's permission to leave a check unresolved. | Extend E17 with a coarse child opening or description; source is a practice/specimen copy, not one of the final April 1854 returns. Do not invent duration, Cut shares, independent qualification, or a completed source resolution. |
| BC-06 | IX / E18 | Prose-only elaboration | Show the scope of Halden's checking narrowing to correct customer particulars while he accepts the known capacity gamble. | Preserve all four acceptances, his sole contracting authority, and the unchanged profile/decision Cuts. |
| BC-07 | X / E20 | Prose-only elaboration | Lovelace searches the existing answers for a usable training date. | No new promise or deadline; preserve deferred expenditure and existing letter-before-visit order. |
| BC-08 | XI / E26 | **Event/evidence refinement** | Wills stops a reading he did not hear; Neale accepts the interruption during their already recorded paired correction. | Extend E26 and the corrective-conduct evidence. Do not treat the episode as independent certification or a new copying error. |
| BC-09 | XII / E29 | Prose-only elaboration | Henry has to turn from imaginable future work to an actual inventory place for the returned table. | Preserve complete custody, both headings, the unresolved general Engine and the 1900 survival-only coda. |

## Minimal proposed model refinements

These statements are proposed authored content, **not changes already applied**:

**E11 — household labor within the credit decision:** Before reading the venture ledger, Margaret asks Edward to let her finish the line in her own stationer's account. He lifts the venture ledger and waits. She then reviews the same unpaid calls and wage obligation already described. The episode opens her work and control of working time without adding income, cost, a new causal shock, or a different decision.

**E17 — supervised source comparison:** During the already recorded practice with Neale, Wills begins from an expected figure made legible in a prepared copy. He then admits he cannot independently read its source. Neale also cannot read it and leaves the check open. Wills asks for the original and marks the unresolved place. This is a practice/specimen source in the existing training period; its later resolution remains unopened. The episode supplies evidence of supervised learning and the ordinary labor of obtaining a trustworthy source. It supplies no independent checker-hours.

**E26 — correction and the permission to interrupt:** In the already recorded four-day paired correction, Wills at first responds to an interruption by rushing the line. Neale returns him to the strip. When their reading and copying roles exchange, Wills makes a second, audible request for a figure he did not hear, and Neale repeats it. The corrected operation remains unchanged. The episode supplies specific evidence for the corrective conduct already carried into his reference.

These descriptions can remain refinements inside the current parent events. Creating separate subsidiary nodes is useful only if the tool or author needs to inspect these episodes independently. No new numerical Cut is needed to justify the prose. If future exploration gives Wills or Margaret richer motives, those should be authored as their attributed understanding and tested against the scene, not inferred from the founders' profiles.

## What should be opened next

The next useful candidate is the ordinary aftermath already accepted in Halden's life: return to salaried estimating after closure. The current manuscript jumps from 1855 to custody in 1871. A small scene could let the reader experience continued work without public redemption, while Margaret and Halden renegotiate household means after his two stakes are lost. This would give the claimed later adaptation evidence beyond the closure decision itself.

That extension is deliberately not written into this candidate. First choose an ordinary job consistent with the existing broad municipal/instrument work, who is present, and what small decision demonstrates changed judgment without simply repeating the wages conversation. Salary, employer, exact year, client and family circumstances remain unestablished. Those choices would require a new or refined post-1855 event before prose. There is no need to invent a famous downstream influence, an Engine Age, or a reconciliation that makes the ending easier.

## Review limits and checks

- Complete accepted manuscript and relevant world/person/scene/health/route/understanding documents were read.
- Source SHA-256, candidate SHA-256 and exact changed block hashes are recorded in the anchor map.
- All twelve headings and the complete ordered sequence of numeric literals match the source. These mechanical checks protect against accidental omission; they do not prove semantic fidelity.
- Manual review checked the main risks introduced by the new prose: the practice source is not a final 1854 return; no completed independent training is claimed; reader/copier role exchanges are explicit; Babbage's drawing does not arrive before his visit; the apparatus configuration, cost, and four-day correction remain fixed.
- Source and model files remain untouched. No native narrative revision, director review, evidence rebind, fresh import, paper rendering or publication has been performed for this candidate. It should not be described as model-validated or final.

2. Halden's 'We gave it' suggests office responsibility. His handwritten authorization to deliver before the second comparison establishes his direct part; he later admits waiving Neale's comparison.

3. Wills transposed and checked against himself; intentional deceit or awareness of the error is not established. Neale was occupied with Lothbury; knowledge of the waiver is unknown. Halden authorized the unchecked delivery, then investigates and discloses; knowing the input was wrong at authorization is not established.

4. Friday wages, returnable £180 and another job's deadline pressure Halden. He could request an extension or move Neale and break the other promise. Instead he deferred comparison until Monday, avoiding a difficult letter and preserving appearances with hands for two and four dates.

5. Davies's response, consequences for the people, repayment, jobs, later contracts, the office's survival and changes to checking remain unresolved. The Returned Table\n\nThe packet came back tied with the office's own green tape.\n\nEdward Halden knew the tape because he had ordered twelve dozen yards of it and\nargued down the price. He knew the paper because its weight had been entered in\nthe delivery account. He knew the seal of Guardian Assurance, pressed too hard\ninto the red wax, and Griffith Davies's narrow hand upon the wrapper. What he\ndid not know was why the packet should have returned unopened at one end and\ncut cleanly along the other.\n\nThe calculating room continued behind him. A shaft turned beneath the floor.\nEvery few seconds the card reader lifted, admitted a stiff rectangle, and let\nit fall into the receiving box. The apparatus did not sound like thought. It\nsounded like six metal cupboards being locked in sequence.\n\nDavies's letter contained three sentences.\n\nThe figures in the enclosed table did not agree with Guardian's independent\ncalculation from age forty-seven onward. The office was to suspend the related\nwork. Mr Davies requested the source sheets, the operation cards, both checking\nsignatures, and an account of the discrepancy under clause eleven.\n\nHalden read the letter twice and placed it flat upon his desk. He did not call\nfor Babbage. He did not yet call for the clerk who had prepared the cards. First\nhe opened the returned table.\n\nThe error was not theatrical. No column descended into nonsense. The values\nremained orderly and plausible; each differed from Guardian's by an amount\nsmall enough to survive an impatient glance and large enough to alter a later\nreserve. That was worse. An absurd answer accused itself. A reasonable wrong\nanswer recruited the reader.\n\nHe took the configuration register from the locked cabinet and checked the\nseal. Unbroken. The mechanism described there was still the mechanism in the\nroom: six signed registers, addition and subtraction, the same transfer order,\nthe same limits they had stated three years before. He found the run trace. It\nshowed no jam, correction, or repeated card. The second run agreed with the\nfirst.\n\nBy noon Babbage stood at the long table with his spectacles in one hand and the\nreturned sheets in the other.\n\n“The recurrence is exact,” he said.\n\n“The table is wrong.”\n\n“Wrong, yes, but see where.” Babbage set down his spectacles and ran one finger\nalong the trace. “The first supplied value. After that, every transfer is true.\nNo wheel introduced this. The Engine carried what it was given.”\n\nHalden knew that relief. He had felt it himself on finding the seal unbroken.\nNow Babbage was looking only at the trace.\n\n“We gave it,” Halden said.\n\n“The preparation desk gave it.”\n\n“That desk is in this office.”\n\nBabbage picked up his spectacles. “Then correct the copy and repeat.”\n\nHalden looked through the glass partition. The preparers sat at facing desks,\nreducing customer sheets to a form the cards could carry. Beyond them, the\napparatus continued its patient sequence. To a visitor the machine was the\nmarvel and the clerks were furniture. The accounts said otherwise. For every\nhour of its operation, people spent several hours deciding what it should be\ngiven, and more deciding whether its answer could leave the room.\n\nHe sent for the Guardian source sheet and the preparation copy. At a quarter\npast one, he found the first divergence. Guardian had supplied 3,742. The\npreparation copy read 3,472. The two middle figures had exchanged places in a\nhand so familiar that Halden recognized it before he read the initials.\n\nSamuel Wills came in pale. He had brought the ruler and pencil from his desk\nalthough Halden had asked only for him; he kept them aligned between his hands\nwhile he stood.\n\n“Did you compare this line with the source?” Halden asked.\n\n“I read the copy back, sir.”\n\n“To whom?”\n\nThe young man looked toward the checking room.\n\n“Mr Neale had the Lothbury packet. I read it back to myself.”\n\n“That is not a comparison.”\n\n“No, sir.”\n\n“Who instructed you to release the cards?”\n\nThe clerk said nothing. The ruler shifted in his hands, and he brought its end\nlevel with the pencil again. Halden had been about to ask the question again,\nlouder. He dismissed him instead.\n\nThe young man took both tools away. Through the partition Halden watched him\nlay them square with the edge of his desk before sitting down. Then Halden\nopened the delivery ledger.\n\nThere should have been two marks beside the Guardian job: the preparer's and an\nindependent checker's. There was one. Beneath it, in the margin reserved for an\nexception, was a short authorization in Halden's own hand.\n\nSecond comparison to follow. Delivery permitted to preserve date.\n\nE. H.\n\nHe remembered the morning. The wages had been due on Friday. Guardian's\ndelivery date fell that day; missing it would make its one hundred and eighty\npounds returnable. Neale had been checking another table whose delay would also\nhave cost the office money. Halden had told himself that a single delivery\ncould borrow two days from its own conditions and repay them on Monday.\n\nHe had seen the other choices. He could have asked Davies for an extension and\nadmitted that the office had sold a date it could not safely keep. He could have\nmoved Neale from the Lothbury packet and broken that promise instead. Or he\ncould let one signature stand temporarily for two and preserve both appearances\nuntil Monday. The third course had felt least like a decision because it moved\nno visible object and required no difficult letter. Only a line in the margin\nhad changed.\n\nMonday had filled itself before it arrived.\n\nBabbage read the authorization without sitting down.\n\n“It remains a human failure,” he said. “The apparatus received three thousand\nfour hundred and seventy-two and treated it with perfect fidelity. To charge\nthe mechanism with the table is to confuse obedience to an operation with\njudgment upon its premise.”\n\n“Of course it is.”\n\nThe answer surprised him. Babbage turned.\n\n“Wills transposed two figures,” Halden continued. “I waived Neale's comparison.\nWe sold four dates with hands for two. Which entry do you want first?”\n\n“You have passed from one supplied value to the constitution of the office.\nThat may be a second inquiry; it is not a failure of the calculating\nmechanism.”\n\n“We took one witnessed trial and sold four tables upon it.”\n\nFor a moment neither man spoke. Through the partition came the fall of another\ncard.\n\nOn the shelf above Halden's desk stood the test packet from 1851, its seals cut\nbut preserved. Beside it lay Lady Lovelace's qualification on capacity. He had\nfiled them together because their paper was the same size. Until that morning\nhe had not admitted that they were parts of the same result.\n\nDavies had asked for both checking signatures. Halden dipped his pen and began\nthe reply with the one fact no calculation could improve.\n\nThere was no second signature."}"},"verdict":"Absolute target recovery is 5/5 for each selected passage. Babbage answered too
quickly. Lovelace laughed—not at him, but because she had wanted the same thing.

Halden, who had entered every paid hour of its construction, let it continue.

nodes.text:
## U01 — Why a third principal exists

Targets: E02--E06; Edward Halden's life.

Babbage and Lovelace can continue a negotiation but cannot, between them,
supply independent manufacture, commercial staging, and liability. The third
principal therefore carries the narrow integration function that makes the
divergence causal. He is fictional because assigning all of that function to a
known historical figure would distort the evidence. He does not absorb the
manufacturer, customer, financier, or successor roles.
nodes.title: U01 — Why a third principal exists

nodes.text:
## U02 — Why the machine is small

Targets: the Bounded Card Apparatus; E03, E06, E14.

A completed general Analytical Engine by 1851 would require far more
counterfactual industrial change than the story needs. A six-register,
addition-and-subtraction, card-directed apparatus gives the founders something
real to finish and test while preserving the distinction between the bounded
artifact and Babbage's architecture. If later technical opening shows even this
configuration to be implausible, reduce its registers or card sequence rather
than enlarging the industrial world to rescue it.
nodes.title: U02 — Why the machine is small

nodes.text:
## U03 — Why success is the central shock

Targets: E14--E18.

Another mechanical failure would merely confirm every existing caution. A
bounded success changes the principals' wants and interpretations in different
directions and creates the temptation the conditions were designed to resist.
It therefore produces both stronger causality and a better story: their method
works, then they misstate what its success licenses.
nodes.title: U03 — Why success is the central shock

nodes.text:
## U04 — Why the office fails outside the mechanism

Targets: E17--E27.

The tested arithmetic should remain true. The office fails because recurring
calculation is a human-machine process containing preparation, checking,
delivery, correction, and money. The known two-job checking capacity, the
four-job commitment, the specific transposition, and the omitted duplicate
check make the failure traceable without making the apparatus magically break
at the required dramatic moment.
nodes.title: U04 — Why the office fails outside the mechanism

nodes.text:
## U05 — Why Lovelace's death is not the cause of the error

Targets: E19--E24.

Her illness and death expose a succession failure already visible in the 1852
capacity review. The surviving principals choose not to fund a second checker
before she dies. Death removes her active pressure; it does not enter a wrong
number or force Halden's later delivery decision. This preserves agency and
avoids using a woman's death as a mechanical plot device.

## U06 — Why the ending is documentary

Targets: E27--E30.

The counterfactual earns one bounded proof, not an industrial revolution. The
complete packet is a meaningful surviving object because it contains success
and failure under the same identity. Babbage's late growth is the decision not
to curate away the parts that limit his preferred interpretation.

## U07 — Revision from the first candidate round

Targets: the whole 07r2 construction.

The earlier candidate passes showed that a plausible macro outcome was not enough:
continued negotiation lacked a person capable of converting it into priced,
staged obligations. This version retains the useful bounded-proof and
overcommitment pattern, adds the missing commercial founder, and narrows the
long-run outcome. Discarded casts, signature objects, prose, and numerical
worlds are not part of this construction.

## U08 — Pragmatic revision rule

Targets: all later openings.

When a finer event is uncertain but does not change the parent account, keep it
coarse or put it in the remainder. When a local route is weak, repair that
route. When the children reveal that the parent could not have happened, or
that the only coherent realization is dramatically inert, revise the parent
and propagate the change. Do not restart a whole world to avoid making an
ordinary authorial choice.

## U09 — Why this world is accepted

Targets: the complete macro, E01--E30, and the twelve-passage route.

Progressive opening found local defects—the access route to Halden, the formal
authority behind the 1852 contracts, and the exact 1854 delivery choice—but no
failure of the parent history. Farrow now supplies the access route, Halden
alone binds the customers after Babbage urges expansion, and the omitted check
has its own Direction Cut. The ledgers close, the prospective test remains
valid, and each principal's late action grows out of an earlier pattern. The
world is therefore accepted at its declared resolution. Unopened workshop,
subscriber, and customer detail stays remainder rather than delaying the book.

## U10 — Why assurance and threat are separated from fear

Targets: the principal period profiles; selected-scene WHAT and FEELS Cuts;
passages I--XII.

The five core wants identify what is receiving motivational attention. They do
not by themselves say whether the person expects those wanted endpoints to be
secured. The added outlook Cut therefore divides one comparable unit between
assured fulfillment, threatened fulfillment, and unresolved expectation; its
threat child may then be opened across the five wanted regions. Fear remains a
separate emotional appraisal because the same represented threat can instead
organize anger, sadness, bargaining, or action. This distinction guided a
small rendering revision: Babbage classifies mechanisms under threat,
Lovelace converts uncertainty into explicit conditions, and Halden moves from
bounded accounting through promotional accounting to self-audit. No world
event or causal dependency changed.

## U11 — Why the emotional-depth pass adds residue rather than shocks

Targets: E09--E11, E14, E18--E28; passages II, V, VII--XII.

The accepted world already contains the required long perturbations: earlier
institutional rupture makes finite dependence threatening to Babbage; bounded
success destabilizes both him and Halden; Lovelace's foreseeable absence tests
whether authority has a carrier; and the returned table forces a slow change in
what counts as the work's complete record. Adding another catastrophe would
weaken that causality. The revision instead repeats existing objects with
changed use—drawings cover ledgers, deposit letters cover the capacity line,
handwriting widens, checking tools wear, and proof and failure remain under one
tape. Explanatory prose was removed where those residues could show adaptation.

nodes.text:
## U12 — Why character refinements change the model before the rendering

Targets: E04, E06, E09, E14, E17, E20, and E26; passages II--XII.

Lovelace's fallibility and the secondary people's lives need consequences beyond
their assigned jobs. The smallest correction does not add a new shock. It opens consequences
already latent in accepted Events. In the finite compact Lovelace declines an
unspecified deputy because substitution could dissolve the rare authority she
has won; in 1852 she recognizes that this protection also made her a single
carrier, which sharpens rather than magically supplies her succession argument.
Davies's curiosity makes evidential restraint a choice, Farrow protects his
foreman's finding despite delayed payment, and Neale tries to teach Wills
without counting supervised practice as independent capacity, then shares
responsibility for the correction. These refinements were entered in the life
and Event descriptions before their passages were revised. They do not alter
the macro outcome or any existing Cut composition. The remaining changes remove
balanced, thesis-bearing speech and replace it with handling, interruption, and
profession-specific language; those are rendering changes rather than new
world facts.

nodes.text:
## U13 — Why invention joy is deepened

Targets: E03, E10, E14, E16, and E18; the finite-invention and
recognition-to-overreach change arcs; passages III, VI, VIII--X.

The rendering moves too quickly from making to governance.
The repair therefore opens experiences already causal in the accepted world.
Halden's reversal from pricing a machine part to pricing an answerable claim is
treated as a cognitive invention; the corrected assembly's first free motion is
allowed to reward several kinds of expertise; and the successful trial is
experienced as shared joy before commercial attention arrives.

The pleasure is not an ornamental scene. E14 changes beliefs about feasibility,
standing, and the value of each participant's work. E16 reinforces those
beliefs. In E18 Babbage and Halden then mistake two judgments moved by the same
success and response for independent confirmation. This was already the
recognition-to-overreach arc; the revision makes its positive shock perceptible.
That common-cause account belongs to the constructor's model and is not given to
Lovelace as an explicit diagnosis in the rendered scene. She can demonstrate
the capacity error without possessing the whole explanation of either man.
Accordingly, only the three immediate post-trial FEELS Cuts change. Their joy
shares rise and their anticipatory shares fall because the named moment is now
fixed after the second complete run and before the first inquiry. WHAT, HOW,
fulfillment outlook, threat, and Direction Cuts remain unchanged.

The same macro history and failure remain. The revision develops four literary
functions—cognitive discovery, pleasure in matter,
shared recognition, and intellectual intimacy under bodily cost—through the
current model's existing Events, relationships, Cuts, and change arcs.

## U14 — Why Lovelace discusses mechanical judgment

Targets: E20 and E20a; E23--E26 and E28; passage X; the valid-computational-claim
concept model.

Lovelace's published 1843 Notes already distinguish the Engine's ability to
follow supplied analytical relations from any power to originate those
relations, while also proposing that suitably represented relations outside
ordinary number—including harmony—could be subjected to operation. Passage X
does not quote the Notes or attribute modern terminology to her. It develops
those documented positions inside the counterfactual self-comparison design.

The exchange changes a record: a common-source fault causes Babbage to narrow
mechanical verification to comparison of internal operations. Lovelace states
only the distinction between an unforeseen consequence and intention.
Guardian's source sheet, followed by the returned table, supplies the adverse
case.

nodes.text:
## U15 — Why voice and sensory detail are consequences of the model

Targets: principal life trajectories; E03, E06, E10, E14, E18, E20--E21, and E26;
passages I--XI.

The voice pass adds no Event, Cut, causal dependency, or outcome. Sentence
movement and diction are derived from the person's existing organization:
Babbage expands from the local question toward architecture, Lovelace translates
between representations and grows terser as bodily capacity declines, and
Halden names hours, money, workers, dates, and deliverables. Secondary voices
use the narrower evidence their work makes available. These are rendering
constraints recorded in `PERSON-MODELS.md`, not new personality coordinates.

Sensory detail is likewise rendered from Things already participating in an
Event and from their changing state: coupled assemblies transmit load, heat,
and vibration; the trial exposes cards, register faces, the slowing shaft, and
the sealed comparison case; the succession episode exposes drawings, breath,
packets, and the cold apparatus. A city or room remains a Place Thing; presence
and any consequential weather, traffic, work, or crowd condition are Events in
its lifecycle. A separate place Event is opened only if that condition changes
access, timing, choice, or consequence. This keeps atmosphere available without
letting an unmodeled detail become a hidden cause.

The final bounded prose pass opens the already recorded deputy refusal and
its later recognition, without adding a successor or changing the plot.
Lovelace hesitates before striking the provision; in illness she asks William
about the signature and admits she would have refused his substitution.
Recognition does not settle her attachment to the authority she secured.
Several narrator explanations are removed where the action already supplies
their meaning, and a few exchanges lose their immediate polished rebuttals.
E06, E20, the person description, and the route retain those same choices.
The Cut weights, accounting, dates, capacity, outcomes, and ending are
unchanged. A fresh retrospective import is required to bind the revised
descriptions and manuscript to their new source identities.

nodes.text:
## U16 - Connect preparation to the final checking window

Targets: E09, E17--E18, E22--E24; passages VI, IX, and X.

A fresh complete-manuscript reading identified a missing link: at forty hours
per packet, four checks appear finishable long before the 1854 delivery unless
the reader knows why the final inputs are not yet available. The world model
already placed all four checks in one delivery quarter. This pass opens that
commitment: methods and specimen work precede customer returns closed at the
end of 1853; final figures arrive in early 1854 for April--June delivery.
Earlier checking cannot certify those new values. This is an authored source
dependency, not a fifth customer, new historical evidence, or new work invented
to consume every intervening hour.

Halden's error remains a gamble on future capacity followed by a refusal to
fund it. The existing 80-hour capacity, 40-hour final check, four contracts,
cash accounts, and decision Cuts are unchanged. The model descriptions and
loadable scaffold request are updated before the prose. The scene then shows
old checking marks being set aside instead of adding a speech about scheduling.

The same reading caught two consecutive Babbage speeches that looked like
alternating speakers in VI. His claim that the failure justifies the larger
redesign is joined into one attributed speech. No character position changes.
The witnessed test, emotional palette, death, closure, and custody ending are
preserved. This pass does not claim a fresh Rust import.

nodes.text:
## U17 - Retrospective Rust import and the final-source cutoff

Targets: E17--E24; passages IX--X; the concept component Cut and person scaffolds.

The construction review distinguished a coherent authored artifact from a
complete native execution record. This repair imports the existing descriptions,
person processes, Cuts, and manuscript into a new database. It records the
source digests and new compilation and retrieval results; it does not recover
earlier editing order. The concept allocation gains an explicit zero remainder
and component addresses. All thirteen declared person profiles now request
their nine concurrent processes. Slow outlook remains authored: unselected
scenes are not invented to manufacture a temporal-mixture proof.

Checking the source schedule exposed a remaining causal weakness in U16's
refinement. Returns available during the first quarter could consume that
quarter's checking hours before April--June. The revised authored arrangement
is that customers reconcile the year-end returns during the first quarter,
then release the final signed checking copies from 1 April 1854. Guardian's
copy arrives on that date; other April arrivals remain coarse. Work on earlier
specimens or provisional figures cannot replace comparison against these final
copies. E22's window extends through April, and the model, route, and two
affected passages carry the same constraint.

This supersedes U16's source-availability assumption, not its preserved account
of the earlier revision. The four jobs, forty hours per final check, eighty
protected quarter-hours, omission on 7 April, refund, closure, and ending do
not change. Nor do the psychological weights. The alteration is a local repair
to the causal explanation, not new historical evidence or a rerolled world.

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s care conflict distinguishes an accurate record from permission to decide for another person. This is an authorial analogy to investigate beside the Book’s existing actions, not an identity between the worlds: Babbage’s exact mechanism claim in I and XI does not settle what the office promised, and Lovelace’s deputy refusal in V protects authority while creating a succession vulnerability. Existing U05 and U12 retain their original account. Future revision should preserve each person’s partly valid position and era-specific powers rather than make Nora’s contemporary lesson their shared speech."}
nodes.title: An accurate account can fail to answer another person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"The ending already names a bounded object: configuration, proof, qualification, error, correction and closure. Nora’s new compositional question is whether faithful custody can leave the people more various than this account of their undertaking. Her own later relapse into planning Kit’s life prevents an easy claim that recognition permanently cures a habit. Preserve Babbage’s impatient last question and Henry’s separate life; do not add a concluding thesis. This is a new interpretation linked to the received ending, not recovered intent."}
nodes.title: Complete of an object, not complete of a person

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s shoulder adaptation and earlier care fatigue supply sensitivity to changing reach, waiting and ordinary dependence. They do not diagnose Lovelace or alter her historical-counterfactual illness. In Chapter X William’s water, the interrupted pencil and the unclosed page can remain distinct from the professional argument. In IX and XI, Neale and Wills’ checking actions acquire different meanings through their own modeled learning. Future voice review must inspect those processes and actual lines separately."}
nodes.title: Bodily limits alter rhythm without settling meaning

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Nora’s tendency to make family time absorb her jobs makes Chapter VII’s interrupted account especially salient. The existing passage already lets Margaret finish her own line before taking Edward’s book. That is a strength to preserve. A future opening should ask what Margaret attends to before and after the exchange and whether it changes a meaningful choice; adding biography or dialogue merely to make her a lecturer would weaken the scene. This remains an open authorial inquiry, not new world canon."}
nodes.title: Margaret’s work has a life beyond correcting Halden

nodes.text: {"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Prospective compositional connection, created 27 September 2026. Nora’s fabrication and singing experiences make her attentive to the real pleasure in Chapter VI’s extra turn and Chapter VIII’s three empty strokes after success. These passages already work through action and sensory attention. The new author model is a reason to preserve and explore their distinct pleasures, not to add a moral after them or claim she caused their existing wording. U13 already records the original construction rationale."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"“One farther” and “You see” let Charles direct attention in the clipped manner of someone tired but still occupied by his work. Henry’s questions and moving of the sheet show participation without promising succession. Their shared technical interest makes the later “Do you?” less tidily resolved. The custody headings and 1900 survival-only ending stand."}

{"schema":"meaning-model-understanding-note/v1","kind":"voice","text":"Margaret’s “Don’t go yet” asks for company after the existing account discussion. “Only one of them has the estate” is a joke inside their reading, not another principle she teaches Edward. Edward’s interrupted errand and dry reply preserve his preoccupation and a small capacity for company. No permanent change in his financial judgment is inferred. The older current-balance note still stands; its question about the later failure remains open."}

These choices realize Nora’s attention to pleasure and physical reach without making her modern biography historical evidence or retroactively crediting her with the prior book."}

The life and role are wholly invented now. The historical third-person narrator remains a separate narrative function.","whyThisStory":"The existing Book puts Nora’s unresolved problem in a world unlike her own: how to keep an answerable record without treating the record as the whole human undertaking. Her fabricated displays, family rota and later physical limits give her reasons to see hidden labor and to distrust her pleasure in a clean account. Its joy in making also challenges her tendency to explain away unproductive pleasure.","teach":"She wants a reader to feel the cost and pleasure of work shared across unequal kinds of knowledge. No settled lesson makes a person complete or proves that refusing a promise is always right.","figuringOut":"Can a record remain complete about a bounded undertaking while leaving a person unexhausted by it? Nora recognizes Halden’s relief in naming the account and Babbage’s wish to protect a true distinction. She has not settled when accuracy is care, when it is self-defense and when a conversation or pleasure matters without entering the account.","lifeRecords":["event:event.nora.first_job","event:event.nora.care_quarrel","event:event.nora.care_adaptation","event:event.nora.choir_return","event:event.nora.kit_departure","event:event.nora.composition","concept:concept.nora.record_as_substitute","concept:concept.nora.shared_pleasure"]},"reader":null,"buttons":[{"id":"truth_without_answer","button":"What if every sentence of my explanation is true and I have still failed someone?","presses":"The mechanism’s exact operations coexist with the office’s broken promise and Halden’s own authorization.","learns":"A reader may notice a question their explanation leaves unanswered; the story does not decide their real case for them.","readerRecords":[]},{"id":"needed_or_known","button":"If others can do without me, what is left of my importance?","presses":"Lovelace’s contested authority and resisted deputy, Neale’s teaching, and Henry’s custody make dependence valuable and dangerous in different ways.","learns":"The fear of substitution can coexist with care; named relationships and circumstances determine its effects.","readerRecords":[]},{"id":"pleasure_survives_failure","button":"Will admitting the failure erase what was wonderful?","presses":"The successful assembly and trial remain joyful and true after the office closes.","learns":"Bounded achievement can retain value without being inflated into a promise it cannot carry.","readerRecords":[]}]},"authoringClock":{"rootId":"story.understanding.a473b1a796dbe8103f32d9fd","unit":"authoring_step","at":11}}
